v1.feedback: The Lorenz butterfly is a clear mathematical shape and the ghost-double mirror is a genuine attempt at 'selcouth' estrangement, but the connection to parent q3x (planes_not_points) is weak — this reads as a fresh Lorenz attractor, not a morphed continuation of the parent. The spatial fold is too subtle at 0.12 amplitude to register as uncanny; crank it or make it temporally episodic so moments of normalcy break into strangeness. The teal-to-amber palette is restrained and works, but the ghost layer at alpha 0.012–0.04 is nearly invisible on most monitors — raise ghost opacity or give it a distinct hue shift so the doubling actually reads. Camera is fixed at z=85 which frames the butterfly well, but a slow drift or breath on the FOV would earn the 'selcouth' brief more than a static viewpoint.

v2.feedback: The episodic fold is a genuine selcouth gesture — the bilateral collapse-and-inversion maps the word onto the parent's butterfly well, and the ghost doubling sells the afterimage uncanniness. However, the palette now carries five-plus distinct hues (indigo, magenta, gold, fold-teal, ghost-cyan-green) which muddies the restrained feel; pick one accent shift for the fold and let the ghost inherit the primary palette at lower saturation instead. Primary alpha floor at 0.025 with additive blending risks washing dense lobe cores to white while leaving the wings too faint — raise the floor to ~0.04 and cap accumulated brightness with a gentle tone-map or switch the ghost layer to normal blending at premultiplied alpha so the silhouette stays crisp rather than blooming into a glow cloud.
